steps.step: Deploy Reserve Vault (Spain pack, general: VAT 21% + income tax 20%)
Deploy Inbox for the vault
Deploy Router
Client pays invoice INV-2027-001 (1,210 KUSD) through the Router
Client sends 121 KUSD to the inbox with a plain SEP-41 transfer
Keeper sweeps the inbox (permissionless)
Expected payment for invoice KYR-2027-003 (base 1,000, VAT 21%, IRPF 15% withheld by the client): the freelancer registers its terms in the vault
The client pays 1,060 KUSD with the invoice reference: the vault applies the invoice terms, not the default rule
steps.detail: freelancer +800, vault +260 (VAT 210, income-tax reserve 50; the default rule would have reserved only 184 of VAT)

steps.step: Freelancer pays the VAT bucket to the tax destination with an anchor-style memo (muxed address, id 4242), before the due date
Freelancer schedules a 50 KUSD income-tax instalment to the tax destination; running it before its time is refused
steps.detail: refused by the contract: NotYet (contract error #32)

steps.step: On its date the keeper runs it (no owner signature): the instalment goes only to the tax destination
Release before the due date is refused
steps.detail: refused by the contract: NotDue (contract error #4)

steps.step: Freelancer proposes a new tax destination (2-minute notice in this demo)
Applying it before the notice has passed is refused
steps.detail: refused by the contract: ChangeNotReady (contract error #8)

steps.step: The guardian finds the proposal by asking the RPC for proposals only
A second payment address for clients abroad: an inbox the vault books without VAT (expect_payer, owner-signed)
A client abroad pays 1,000 KUSD to that address: no VAT reserved, income tax as usual
The same client then pays 1,210 KUSD to the usual address: 210 of VAT is reserved, and the app recognises the wallet from its payment to the address for clients abroad
steps.detail: payer GA3EZPL7… seen paying both addresses

steps.step: The owner proposes taking that VAT back (210 KUSD); applying it before the 2-minute notice is refused
steps.detail: refused by the contract: NotYet (contract error #32)

steps.step: The owner registers the client wallet's terms: its next payment through the Router reserves no VAT
One payment address per client: the same wallet pays 1,210 KUSD to a client-at-home address and 1,000 KUSD to an EU business address, swept in one tick; VAT is reserved only for the first
steps.detail: VAT reserved: 210 (21% at home: 210; reverse charge: 0); addresses CBWCLLAWLS2I6G23YCLNOQKCE2AJVFLSDJCZCXKWBQJRZPJOFRMK3DZK, CD57XYCIBA2ZFFUISJ4QKGAXVGSZ2J4FOWBHSN6CTCTAFE4M2TJDTID2

steps.step: Public money: a vault proposes accepting KCB, a test digital dollar issued like a central bank's (authorization required, freeze and clawback enabled); before the 2-minute notice a payment in it is refused
steps.detail: refused by the contract: TokenNotAccepted (contract error #3); vault CBXIMA2JJIEG2NT2G7LNJ3INXZC522SKFSG6AGJLEDZDGOR576BK6BJK, asset CDSBXRP6YJ25GAB6RGMOWTSZOFF3IYREH5CPWO5CON53HIOHEMKOHOAJ

steps.step: Fixed fee and payout address: the owner proposes setting aside 100 KUSD per period before the net amount goes out, and paying the net amount to another wallet of theirs (2-minute notice)
steps.detail: propose_fixed c792528682…; until the notice ends the net amount still goes to the signing wallet (vault CD2HWASHQM24LRRAI3L4EQ4DXFUMD2I5XFWXFFRGRRHAAXSR66SHKAHZ)

steps.step: Reserve without income: the owner deposits the 21 KUSD of VAT on 121 received in another wallet; the vault holds it like any reserve, and the period's income stays 0
Euro reserve: a vault taking KUSD and KEUR proposes converting its reserve to KEUR through the Soroswap testnet router (2-minute notice)
steps.detail: Reflector testnet EUR = 1.1080995 USD (price 290s old); pool 1,160,000 KUSD / 1046837.36 KEUR; swapper CATUK52W32ELBHIJ5JJEX23I4SE4DTVZFECEH6JTBEA66J5KRBV5DMXM; vault CBSRCABLEXA6K3K3P3D3P4XLDRJOWJRKCVTLGI7GGP2MDKSPBWIV53PN

steps.step: Thailand vault: the owner signs the scheduled VAT change (7% to 10%) ahead of its date with propose_rule_at
steps.detail: VAT changes from 7% to 10% on 2027-10-01: sign once and the vault switches that day. Demo date: 2026-11-13T08:27:44.000Z; before it, 1,070 still splits as VAT 70 (vault CANBJMUVQQJXNUZDS3Y45QZAJTGBQO3ND5ZFIAX2H3Z2UKVAAZRO7FGP)

steps.step: Rate Registry deployed and seeded from the Spain rule pack (21%); the Spanish vault follows ES/standard, ceiling 25%
The registry publishes a VAT change (demo: 21% to 22%), at least its 2-minute notice ahead
steps.detail: applies from 2026-11-13T08:28:05.000Z; until then the vault still charges 21%

steps.step: Germany: the owner sets the income-tax due date from the tax office's notice (set_due); a later date applies at once, moved past the weekend
An earlier date that would open the lock within the notice period is refused
steps.detail: refused by the contract: DueTooSoon (contract error #30)

steps.step: The owner moves to Germany: a vault from the German pack, and propose_vault on the same inbox (2-minute notice)
steps.detail: new vault CCU7H53J4VQXL3BJ5TUSJIKO3AHPG7KB6UYFTFTRO6MIFPTUI7KICMXJ; 5 steps in the plan; until the notice ends the inbox still pays the Spanish vault

steps.step: After the due date the rest of the period is released to the freelancer
After the notice the keeper applies the correction (no owner signature): the VAT not owed goes back to the freelancer
After the notice a client pays 1,210 KUSD to the inbox: 100 go to the fixed fee first, the other 700 of the net amount to the payout address, nothing to the signing wallet
steps.detail: payout address +700, vault +510 (VAT 210, income tax 200, fixed fee 100)

steps.step: Once the period's fee is set aside, the next payment (121 KUSD) splits as usual: 80 to the payout address
A client pays 1,210 KCB to the inbox; until the issuer authorizes the vault to hold KCB, the sweep fails and the money waits in the inbox
Once the issuer authorizes the vault, the sweep splits the 1,210 KCB: 800 to the freelancer, 410 kept in the vault in KCB
The VAT is paid in KCB straight to the tax office's Stellar account: no anchor, no conversion
Germany: VAT 19% + income tax reserve 30%: 1190 KUSD paid through the same Router
United States: no VAT, federal and self-employment reserve 30%: 1000 KUSD paid through the same Router
United Arab Emirates: VAT 5%, no income tax: 1050 KUSD paid through the same Router
After the change time the same vault charges 10% VAT on its own, with no new signature
steps.detail: 1,100 KUSD: net 800, VAT 100, income tax reserve 200

steps.step: A platform pays two freelancers in one call (pay_many); each payment is split by its own vault
steps.detail: 121 KUSD to the Spanish vault (reserve 41.6557377), 110 KUSD to the Thai vault (reserve 30)

steps.step: After the legal date the Spanish vault charges 22% on its own: the owner signed nothing
After the notice the same inbox pays into the German vault (19% VAT + 30% reserve); the Spanish vault keeps what it holds
steps.detail: 1,190 KUSD to the inbox: German vault +490 (VAT 190, reserve 300)

steps.step: A client pays 1,210 KUSD; the keeper converts the 410 reserve to KEUR through Soroswap, at no less than the oracle price minus 1%
steps.detail: 368.7629038 KEUR (oracle fair value 370.00286): VAT 188.8785605, income tax 179.8843433

steps.step: Vault history read back from contract events and exported as CSV
